title: Microsoft Blames Nine-Hour Microsoft 365 Outage on Maintenance Overload
excerpt: Teams, Outlook, SharePoint, Xbox Live and other services went dark across North America after a backup system buckled under the load of a routine maintenance window.
body:
• Microsoft 365 services including Teams, Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Copilot, and Xbox Live were disrupted for over nine hours on July 23
  • The outage was caused by a backup system overloading while primary infrastructure was down for maintenance
  • A targeted load-balancing fix Microsoft deployed during recovery accidentally made things worse before resolution
  • This is the third major Microsoft 365 outage in 2026, following incidents in January and April

Microsoft 365 suffered its third major outage of the year on Wednesday, leaving millions of enterprise users without access to core productivity tools for more than nine hours after a routine maintenance operation went sideways.

The disruption began at approximately 2:44 PM UTC on July 23, when users across North America started reporting failures in Teams, Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Copilot, Azure, Xbox Live, and the Microsoft Store. Downdetector logged thousands of reports within the first hour.

What Went Wrong

In a post-incident update, Microsoft attributed the outage to “elevated service load resulting from reduced capacity during maintenance for a subset of North America hosted infrastructure.” In simpler terms: the backup system was overwhelmed while the primary system was down for scheduled work.

The company’s attempt to speed up recovery made things worse. Microsoft said it introduced a “targeted load balancing configuration change intended to expedite the recovery process, which incidentally introduced additional traffic imbalances.”

“It looks like the backup system was overloaded, and it brought the system down while they were still doing maintenance on the main system.”

— David Stinner, president of US itek

The Scale of Disruption

The outage hit at the start of the business day on the US East Coast, disrupting workflows for enterprises that depend on Microsoft’s cloud suite for email, video calls, file storage, and collaboration. Xbox Live also went down, affecting gamers.

Microsoft confirmed at 11:12 PM ET — more than 12 hours after the first reports — that “the issue has been mitigated.” The company said it completed reverting the networking update and that telemetry indicated resolution had reached “the vast majority of users.”

A Pattern of Disruptions

The July outage marks the third significant Microsoft 365 disruption in 2026. A January incident affected thousands of users for several hours, and an April outage knocked out Outlook for an extended period. The recurring failures raise questions about Microsoft’s infrastructure resilience at a time when the company is investing heavily in AI capabilities like Copilot.

Impact on Indian Tech Workers

For the roughly 1.5 million Indian IT professionals working across US time zones — many of them supporting Microsoft-dependent enterprise clients — the outage translated into lost productivity and frantic workarounds. Indian IT services giants like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro, which manage Microsoft 365 deployments for global clients, faced a surge of support tickets with no ability to resolve the underlying issue.

The outage also underscores the concentration risk of enterprise dependence on a single cloud provider, a concern that Indian CIOs and IT leaders have increasingly flagged in boardroom discussions about digital resilience.
